That didn't happen. But now Lucas Aagi has destroyed the equilibrium, giving him access to wealth, allowing him to quickly overwhelm other city states. At this time, these city states call for help from mercenaries—the Aadians—who will come and conquer the entire region, establishing an empire called the Aadian Empire led by Sara. As this new empire reaches equilibrium, talent will flow elsewhere, energizing another region.

The Babylonians will then rise, followed eventually by the Assyrians, who come from the Zagros mountains as a new people called the Persians. Remember, the Persians have a religion called Zerass and will conquer all this area, expanding outwards to control Anatolia and Egypt. At this point in history, a new border area called Greece emerges, including Athens and Sparta. The Greeks encounter Persia when Persian mercenaries are sent to help them, bringing back Persian war tactics to Greece. Through piracy, the Greeks gain wealth, forcing the Persians to invade Greece to stop it.

Again, throughout history, margins get wealthy by committing piracy because why not? So now the empire is forced to invade Greece and loses. Unimaginable: some barbarians, the Greeks, defeat the vast Persian Empire, the world's first great world empire. This happens because borderlands have three advantages—energy, openness, and cohesion—that counteract an empire’s mass organization, death, and centralization.

In the empire, people are mostly slaves, working hard but lacking energy. The empire is stagnant, insular, and divided. Conversely, the Greeks work hard, fear no death, learn from others, and remain united. Thus, throughout human history, borderlands conquer empires. When Persians invade Greece, they get defeated, making Greece a major power.

In Greece, innovation centers around Homer, probably the greatest poet in human history, who wrote the Iliad and Odyssey, founding texts of Greek civilization. The alphabet allows Greeks to write down their thoughts quickly, transmitting them widely. Additionally, the polis system, involving all citizens in politics with thousands participating, especially in Athens and Sparta, drives innovation.
